detaileddescription.para: This is used to generate an "argument unused" warning (without clang::driver::options::TargetSpecific) or "unsupported option" error (with TargetSpecific).

briefdescription.para: Used by an unclaimed option with the TargetSpecific flag.

detaileddescription.para: If set, report an "argument unused" warning instead of an "unsupported option" error.

briefdescription.para: Does this argument own its values?
The argument values, as C strings.
If this arg was created through an alias, this is the original alias arg.

detaileddescription.para: For example, *this might be "-finput-charset=utf-8" and Alias might point to an arg representing "/source-charset:utf-8".

briefdescription.para: Returns the used prefix and name of the option: For --foo=bar, returns --foo=.

detaileddescription.para:
This is often the wrong function to call:
Use getValue() to get bar.
Use getAsString() to get a string suitable for printing an Arg in a diagnostic.

briefdescription.para: Return the base argument which generated this arg.

detaileddescription.para: This is either the argument itself or the argument it was derived from during tool chain specific argument translation.

briefdescription.para: Args are converted to their unaliased form.

detaileddescription.para: For args that originally came from an alias, this returns the alias the arg was produced from.

briefdescription.para: Append the argument onto the given array as strings.
Append the argument, render as an input, onto the given array as strings.

detaileddescription.para: The distinction is that some options only render their values when rendered as a input (e.g., Xlinker).

briefdescription.para: Return a formatted version of the argument and its values, for diagnostics.

detaileddescription.para: Since this is for diagnostics, if this Arg was produced through an alias, this returns the string representation of the alias that the user wrote.

briefdescription.para: A concrete instance of a particular driver option.

detaileddescription.para: The Arg class encodes just enough information to be able to derive the argument values efficiently.
